column1: # Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> English source text <TAB> translation
#   context  usually empty. `@plural`, `@id` and `@msg` mean something to the apps; any other
#            word is a label that tells apart two meanings of the same English.
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns (in any
#            order), and a trailing "…" in one needs one in the other.
#   @plural  English `one|other`; the translation lists this language's plural forms, `|`-separated.
#   Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A missing entry shows in English.
# Clean room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English text in ordinary
# computing vocabulary. No other product's localisation, string table or translated UI was
# consulted or copied; add entries the same way.

column3: Nell'intervallo è cambiato di {change}: entro ciò che il solo caso potrebbe produrre.

column2: Add a unit at the busiest task or pool until enough replications meet a target. The answer with every time at its mean is shown too; it is usually too small.

column2: Each analysis runs the experiment several times with the same seed, so the differences come from the change, not from chance. They can take a while.

column2: Each entity takes the first of these that can be met now, all at once, and gives the units back when it leaves.

column2: Each entity waits here at most a time drawn for it as it arrives, then gives up: it takes the way out marked Abandoned, or leaves the model.

column2: Entities that give up waiting take this flow (to try again later, say); the others take the task's other way out.
